context.why: When a file cannot be imported, the person uploading it has to be told what to fix in the language of the spreadsheet in front of them. The team includes student helpers and people passing through for a semester, and a message they cannot act on turns into a support request for whoever maintains the portal. The check and the report builder already exist; this story is how a failing check reads on the page, and the loop back to a corrected file.
context.environment: Python 3.13 via Poetry, virtualenv already synced. Prefix commands with `poetry run`. Tests: `poetry run pytest`. Lint gate: `poetry run pre-commit run -a`, never raw ruff. A development server is already running from this worktree on 0.0.0.0:8001 with the autoreloader; do not start another and do not stop it.
spec_sections: spec.md User Story 4 and its five acceptance scenarios
plan_sections: research.md 'The blocker nothing here can fix'
prior_decisions: FR-012 is the point of this story: every failure names the row, the column heading AS THE TEMPLATE SPELLS IT, and a specific reason. A bare 'invalid value' is a failing test, not a message.

The template the team uses today carries two misspelled column headings that ADR 0003 refuses, so a real file is refused on its header. That refusal is correct and stays. What this story owes it is a message that says plainly the template is out of date, because that is what puts the correction in front of the people who can make it.
FR-013: no internal field name, model name or traceback reaches the reader. Assert it against a deny list rather than trusting review.
D7: every submitted file is kept. Re-uploading after a failure adds a submission, it does not replace one.
D16/#367: the DEBUG=False chrome defect is upstream and not yours. Scope granted-path tests as the earlier stories did.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a file whose rows carry failures, When the check report renders, Then every failure is listed with its row number, the template's own column heading and the specific reason, asserted against the rendered HTML. A vocabulary failure names the supplied value and the vocabulary it failed against.

Given a file whose header is not the official template's — including one carrying the two misspellings ADR 0003 refuses — When it is checked, Then it is refused on the header alone, no row-level failures are reported, and the message says the template is out of date rather than quoting a column name at a reader who cannot act on it.

Given an assessment whose last submission failed, When a corrected file is uploaded against it, Then the new file is checked afresh, the previous report does not persist anywhere on the page, and the earlier submission is still retrievable.
Given any failure report this story can produce, When its rendered text is checked against a deny list of internal field names, model names and traceback markers, Then none appears.

verified_base.note: Every step green, full suite about 85 seconds. Nothing is known-red at this commit. If anything is red when you arrive, STOP and report rather than fixing it.

prohibitions: Stage explicit paths only. Never `git add -A` or `git add .` — this worktree is shared with a running development server and the orchestrator.
Do not stop, restart or start a development server. One is already running on port 8001 with the autoreloader.
Do not relax or work around the header refusal. It is a decision, not a defect, and the team's current template is supposed to fail it.
Never pass dry_run=True to either import resource.
Never weaken or delete a test you did not author in this story.
Do not build the visibility rules or the curator queue. Those are US-5 and US-6.
Do not attempt to fix the DEBUG=False chrome defect; it is raised upstream as django-mvp/django-mvp#367.
Do not add any new dependency.
Do not push, open pull requests or comment on GitHub. Commit locally only.
Never judge layout or appearance from a screenshot and never claim a visual result is correct on that basis.
